GPT-6.2 Astra (Max) by @OpenAI ranks #6 on the Agent Arena Index, one place above GPT-6 Astra (Max). 
However, these models excel in very different capabilities. Let’s dive in by index.

GPT-6.2 Astra vs GPT-6 Astra across key Agent Arena Indexes:
- Coding: 1,338 vs 1,288 (+50)
- Work: 1,280 vs 1,267 (+13)
- Chat: 1,211 vs 1,265 (-54)

This shows the new model’s gain is in coding, where GPT-6.2 Astra climbs from #8 to #3. On Chat, the everyday tasks such as research, tutoring or writing, it drops from #8 to #11. The two shifts nearly cancel out in the overall score.

4.5 years later, riemann hypothesis got solved

but so far openai hasn’t said a single thing about it, because it’s anthropic that solved it

when can we set aside the differences and the ego, and just celebrate great achievements together as humankind?

To be clear, much of what I said has been said by the leaders of other labs. What I *am* saying is this path is not inevitable.

I am saying leaders and leadership matter more than ever, and that’s why I’m proud of the work that Mark and I have done at Meta to put safety as a top focus of our efforts, including delaying the launch of Muse for months and being a leader on the SI Accords that all of our peers have signed onto. We are investing more in safety every day, and have implemented rigorous processes to make sure every step we take is safe and positive. Mark has also called for all labs (including our own) to deploy the vast majority of compute towards serving people and customers rather than towards recursive self-improvement (RSI).

Superintelligence is Arriving

Superintelligence is arriving. How humanity acts over the next year will have great consequence on what future world we live in.

As someone who has spent much of my life in math and science, I see the proof of the Riemann Hypothesis as clearly marking the beginning of a significant change. For most who have studied math, this represents the absolute pinnacle of intellectual accomplishment—nothing humanity has ever accomplished compares to proving the Riemann Hypothesis in terms of sheer intellectual might and strength. As someone who grew up in Los Alamos, New Mexico, many physicists would agree that the discovery of the atomic bomb is a homework problem compared to the Riemann Hypothesis. It is hard to overstate the magnitude of discovery that we have just witnessed—completed with the help of an alien mind that we don’t understand.

For those who did math competitions, there was a similar moment of “oh shit everything is about to change” when the models began acing the AIME in December 2024 with o3. The hardest AIME problems are much harder in terms of sheer intellectual difficulty than the problems that even the most advanced engineers and business people need to solve on a day-to-day basis. There of course is domain-specific knowledge, context, know-how, and other tactical constraints that were needed to unlock the models across other areas, but lack of raw intelligence was not the bottleneck. And in fact, the progress across other domains over the past 2 years as we’ve mitigated these non-intelligence factors has been immense—we have seen coding be nearly solved, the emergence of extremely powerful cyber capabilities, and strong agentic capabilities which have enabled the models to become general-purpose useful aides. Again the key insight here was simply that the hardest AIME problems are intellectually very difficult, far more difficult than most coding work, most cyber work, most business work, etc., and over the past two years we have been filling in the gaps to enable the models to accomplish those things.

To be clear, AIME is an extracurricular activity for teenagers; the Riemann Hypothesis may be the most intellectually demanding problem humanity has ever devised, which some of the most brilliant humans over the past 150 years have dedicated their lives to. At MIT, my professors would have said the hardest intellectual problems in nearly every major field of human study are “easier” than the Riemann Hypothesis, albeit with other challenges such as experimentation, data, and feedback loops. The remaining gaps for models to greatly surpass humanity in every field are no longer intelligence; they are domain-specific know-how, plumbing, and experimentation. This means it is likely that AI will become the greatest contributor of progress across nearly every field, vastly outperforming the best humans.

Notably, this is likely true of AI research. Most researchers would agree that AI research is certainly much less intellectually demanding than solving the Riemann Hypothesis. The models are clearly going to be intelligent enough to automate all of AI research and be clearly superhuman at improving themselves—along with massively accelerating biological research, weapons research, economics research, and more.  The implications are enormous.  In the same way that the math community has not fully digested the proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, nearly every field could be accelerated at a pace beyond what humans can understand or monitor. It is now incredibly important for us to be thoughtful about the future we want and how we get there. It is hard to imagine a world where humanity can maintain control over fully unconstrained recursive self-improvement. It is equally hard to imagine a world where humanity maintains control with superintelligence that is 1000x smarter and more capable than humans in every field.

Now that we are at a point where the scientific and technical problems on capability progress are likely solved, we must not only make progress in the extremely urgent areas of safety, alignment, and security, but we have to start thinking through how we progress thoughtfully. I notice a particular form of lazy thinking within the AI industry, which is that ASI is inevitable and the only problem to solve is how to do it safely, but there is much more at stake. We should not be okay with a “handover” of society to AI. We should endeavor ourselves to build a technology which delivers a positive future for humanity, where all humans have greater agency and empowerment. I strongly believe this is possible, but likely involves the whole industry taking meaningfully different actions from the “default path” in front of us.
